#1571. Liberia vs Cape Verde - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 16 Nov 2026 00:32

Bottom-placed Liberia host Cape Verde in a Group K fixture of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex in Monrovia on Tuesday.

The first leg in Praia on November 13 finished 4-2 to Cape Verde, which lifted the Blue Sharks to three points in third place in a group where only the top two qualify, left Liberia on zero, and kept Mali on nine points and Rwanda on six above them.

The Lone Stars sit bottom of Group K with no points from three matches, having scored three goals and conceded eight, a goal difference of -5 that leaves them six points behind second-placed Rwanda with nine still available.

Mohammed Adil Erradi, the Belgian-Moroccan appointed on a three-year contract on May 18, has yet to win a competitive match as Liberia coach, and a group calling itself the Concerned Stakeholders for Liberian Football Development demanded his dismissal on October 9, according to the Liberian Observer, citing a salary budgeted at US$98,450 a year.

The campaign opened with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali on September 25, where Sylvanus Nimely scored the only Liberian goal, and four days later Mali won 1-0 at this ground through Martial Tia’s 79th-minute strike after goalkeeper Tommy Songo pulled out of the starting line-up during the warm-up.

In Praia on November 13 Liberia trailed 3-1 after 43 minutes, with Franklin Nyenetue’s 36th-minute equaliser cancelled out two minutes later by a corner-kick header from Dje Tavares, before Ayouba Kosiah converted a stoppage-time penalty to set the final score at 4-2.

Liberia’s back three of Jamal Arago, Sampson Dweh and Emmanuel Fully conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse in the first leg, and the defence has now shipped eight goals in three qualifiers, an average of 2.67 per match.

The head-to-head record leans away from the hosts, as Liberia have lost their last three meetings with Cape Verde (2-1 in Accra on October 7, 2021, 1-0 in Mindelo on October 10, 2021, and 4-2 on November 13), although both of their wins in the series came in Monrovia, 3-0 in July 2000 and 1-0 on June 5, 2011.

A post shared by Liberia Men's National Teams (@lbr_lonestar)

Cape Verde arrive third in Group K on three points with a goal difference of -1 (six scored, seven conceded), and a win in Monrovia would take them to six, level with the total currently held by second-placed Rwanda, who host Mali in Kigali at the same 7pm GMT kick-off.

The Blue Sharks drew all three of their World Cup group matches in June (0-0 against Spain, 2-2 against Uruguay and 0-0 against Saudi Arabia) to reach the Round of 32 on their tournament debut, where Argentina beat them 3-2 after extra time on July 3, a 111th-minute own goal from Diney Borges settling it after Deroy Duarte and Sidny Lopes Cabral had pulled Cape Verde level twice.

Bubista then left to coach Moroccan club RS Berkane, and Humberto Bettencourt, his assistant for six years, was promoted on August 19, with his first two qualifiers producing a 3-1 defeat at Mali on September 25 and a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda on September 29.

Those results extended a winless run to six matches, counting the World Cup (three draws and three defeats), which ended in Praia when Ayoni Santos, Dje Tavares, Dailon Livramento and substitute Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored in the 4-2 win, Bettencourt’s first victory in charge.

Cape Verde have conceded in all three of their qualifiers, seven goals at 2.33 per match, compared with five conceded across four World Cup matches, two of which were clean sheets against Spain and Saudi Arabia.

Bettencourt brought in six players for the double-header, among them David Moreira, Yuran Fernandes, Leandro Andrade, Ieltsin Camoes and Sanches Fernandes, and three of the four scorers in Praia (Santos, Tavares and Sanches Fernandes) were finding the net for the senior side for the first time.

Liberia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Cape Verde Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Liberia captain Oscar Dorley, the Al-Taawoun midfielder, is out with a hamstring injury and was left out of Erradi’s 24-man squad, while goalkeeper Derrick Julu of Niger Tornadoes was recalled to replace Songo, who has not featured since withdrawing from the Mali line-up on September 29.

Julu replaced Ashley Williams at half time in Praia, and Erradi said afterwards that Williams, who had played well against Mali, was not at his best, which points to Julu starting in goal on Tuesday.

Nyenetue, who plays for Ranheim, scored the equaliser in Praia and was replaced by William Gibson after 64 minutes with no injury reported.

Without Dorley, Nohan Kenneh and Solomon Tweh are the likeliest holding pairing in a four-man midfield that also used Edward Ledlum and Divine Teah of Slavia Prague, with Sampson Dweh of Viktoria Plzen anchoring the back three.

For the visitors, defender Wagner Pina, who had joined the training camp in Portugal, did not travel to Cape Verde for the first leg, and Bettencourt wished him a quick recovery.

The 26-man squad named on November 4 includes Vozinha, 40, defenders Logan Costa and Lopes Cabral, midfielder Jamiro Monteiro and 36-year-old captain Ryan Mendes, although Lopes Cabral was replaced at half time in Praia by Steven Moreira and the reason has not been given.

Bettencourt could keep the 4-1-4-1 that scored four in Praia, with Deroy Duarte shielding the back four, and he used all five substitutions there (Moreira, Monteiro, Laros Duarte, Sanches Fernandes and Camoes), which leaves a bench that is already familiar with the plan.

Julu; Fully, Dweh, Jamal, Nimely; Ledlum, Tweh, Kenneh, Nyenetue; Teah, Kosiah

Vozinha; J. Paulo, Diney, Costa, L. Cabral; D. Duarte; Mendes, Tavares, Santos, Varela; Livramento

The first leg showed where this tie will be decided, as Liberia conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse inside 43 minutes, and with Dorley absent and Erradi having already changed goalkeepers at half time, he has fewer ways to repair that in four days than Bettencourt has to exploit it again.

Liberia deserve credit for scoring twice in Praia and for restricting Mali to a 79th-minute winner on the synthetic surface at this ground, and both of their wins over Cape Verde came in Monrovia, but the later of them is 15 years old and Cape Verde’s own record of conceding in every qualifier gives the hosts a route to one goal, which is why 1-2 is a better call than a repeat of the four-goal margin.

A Cape Verde win would lift them to six points, which only equals Rwanda’s tally if the Amavubi lose to Mali in Kigali on the same evening, so Bettencourt’s side cannot treat the second leg as a formality.

#1569. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk

In fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their big summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

"It's a GEM" 💎 A beautiful strike from Jérémy Doku to double Man City's lead! https://t.co/lCUFfQmdLC

There were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

“Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

“There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club,” he writes. “We will not give them that opportunity.”

With the football world still making sense of the news, Tony Pulis admits to feeling “cheated”. His Stoke City side were defeated by Manchester City in the 2011 FA Cup final, during the 2009-23 period.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali then likens City’s transgressions to “doping” before Mauricio Pochettino, whose Spurs side were often in the hunt with City for major trophies during his time as manager, says that football has “lived through a period of deception”.

The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It also discloses that image rights had been inflated and key witnesses had lied.

Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group, appears helpless when questioned about the verdict’s findings at the European Football Clubs’ general assembly in Copenhagen by Sky News.

An unblinking Soriano then features in a video statement published by City in which he claimed their guilty verdict was based on “a single false accusation”.

With City on the ropes, Pep Guardiola releases a statement in support of his former club, assuring supporters that “we will get through this together”.

The Prime Minister says that he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners, but after significant backlash, No 10 moves to clarify his reaction saying that “if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences”.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1567. Jordan vs Australia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 08:05

Jordan and Australia will face off in a rare November international friendly at Suheim Bin Hamad Stadium in Doha on Tuesday.

The home side are striving for consistency following their group-stage exit from the 2026 World Cup, while Australia will be looking to make it back-to-back away victories.

Jordan may have fallen short of the group-stage hurdle at their first-ever World Cup, but they still produced some memorable moments for their supporters.

Despite suffering a 3-1 defeat to Austria in their opening game, Ali Olwan's stunning strike remains fresh in the memory.

Jordan failed to win either of their remaining matches against Algeria and Argentina, but they showed no shortage of fighting spirit before their World Cup campaign came to an end.

Badou Zaki's side are now without a win in their last 10 matches and have recorded two draws since the tournament.

The Chivalrous Ones played out a 1-1 draw against Syria in their first match after the World Cup in September before being held to a goalless stalemate by Venezuela in October, extending their winless run through two underwhelming friendlies.

In contrast, Australia enjoyed a memorable tournament, reaching the knockout stages despite being drawn in a difficult group.

Tony Popovic's side stunned many with a 2-0 victory over a strong Turkey outfit in their opening match.

They subsequently lost 2-0 to the USA, but a goalless draw was enough to secure their passage into the knockout rounds, where they suffered a 4-2 penalty shootout defeat to Egypt after the match finished 1-1 in normal time.

Australia faced Brazil twice in international friendlies after the World Cup, drawing 1-1 in the first encounter before losing 4-2 in the return fixture.

However, they head into this contest with renewed confidence after thrashing Qatar 3-0 earlier this week, with all three goals arriving in the first half.

Zaki has a fully fit squad at his disposal, and it will be interesting to see which combination he opts for.

Abdallah Al-Fakhouri could retain his place in goal, although Alec Samir featured in the 1-1 draw against Syria.

World Cup hero Mousa Al-Tamari is expected to lead the attack alongside Olwan and veteran forward Mahmoud Al-Mardi.

Australia, meanwhile, are missing several key players, with Cameron Burgess ruled out by a cruciate ligament injury and Jordan Bos also sidelined with a knee problem.

The Socceroos are also without skipper Mathew Ryan and fellow veterans Jackson Irvine and Milos Degenek, plus midfielder Aiden O'Neill, but it unclear whether they made themselves unavailable for safety reasons.

Diesel Herrington, Thomas Waddingham and Sam Klein are new call-ups, while striker Kusini Yengi joins brother Tete Yengi, while goalkeepers Joe Gauci and Tom Glover have been recalled.

Al-Fakhouri; Badawi, Nasib, Rousan, Taha; Sadeh, Al-Rawabdeh, Qashi; Tamari, Olwan, Al-Mardi

Beach; Kasey Bos, Herrington, Souttar, Circati, Italiano; McGree, Metcalfe, Okon-Engstler; Irankunda, Yengi

Jordan will be desperate to secure their first victory since 2025 and should fancy their chances against an Australian side missing several key players. However, the visitors will be keen to end the international break unbeaten, and we expect an entertaining contest to finish level.

#1566. Arsenal targeting ‘prolific’ Serie A striker as Napoli and Benfica enter the picture

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Arsenal are reportedly among the clubs keeping a close eye on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, whose outstanding start to the season has attracted interest from several major European sides.

The 21-year-old Portuguese forward has emerged as one of Serie A’s most exciting attacking prospects, with his goalscoring form reportedly putting him on the radar of Arsenal, Napoli and former club Benfica.

According to ⁠Calciomercato.it, Napoli could look to make a move for Varela during the January transfer window as they assess their attacking options.

However, Arsenal are also among the clubs monitoring the striker, with the Premier League side representing a significant threat to Napoli’s plans. Benfica are another interested party after allowing Varela to leave for Monza last summer.

Varela has scored seven goals in eight Serie A appearances, placing him at the top of the league’s goalscoring standings at the time of the report. His performances have helped establish him as a player attracting attention beyond Italy.

The forward joined Monza from Benfica in the summer, and his immediate impact has made the transfer look increasingly valuable for the Italian club.

Although Benfica no longer have Varela under contract, they reportedly retained the right to match a future offer for the striker, alongside a 20 per cent share of any profit Monza makes from a subsequent sale.

That arrangement could complicate negotiations for Arsenal or Napoli, although it does not automatically mean Benfica will bring the player back to Portugal.

Napoli could explore a January approach, while Benfica’s contractual rights give them a potential role in any future deal.

What this means for Arsenal: Varela is a name worth watching as the transfer window approaches, but any potential move will depend on Monza’s willingness to negotiate and the level of competition from Napoli and Benfica. #1565. Peter Schmeichel fumes at Man United for 'very disrespectful' treatment of Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on Old Trafford job - with club legend put out of his misery on Thursday

Published: 15:20 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 12 November 2026

Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford.

The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco.

Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake.

But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position.

'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel said on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong.

Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected.

'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.'

Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August.

Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford.

But to Schmeichel, the issue lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself.

'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender.

'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed.

'Now, was Michael Carrick in on those decisions? Well, it took them forever, forever, to give him the job. So, I suspect he wasn’t in any of those discussions about who to sign up until the point he got named as manager.

Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning

The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future

'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.'

By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United.

The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer.

But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his issue is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout.

'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that?

'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.'

Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club.

'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people.

'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.'

Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm.

Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa.

In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence.

'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he said. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

#1563. Poland vs Sweden - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 01:18

Fighting for a chance at survival in UEFA Nations League B, Poland will welcome Group B4 winners Sweden to Tarczynski Arena on Tuesday.

The Eagles are under pressure, though the Blue and Yellow have already clinched top spot and could be caught off guard.

Jan Urban's Poland have endured a dire campaign so far, and the best they can hope for at this stage is to qualify for the League B/C playoffs.

The Eagles only required a draw against Romania last time out to secure a place in an inter-division showdown, but they were beaten 2-1 in Bucharest on Saturday.

That defeat has left Urban's side third in Group B4 with four points to their name, just one clear of Romania ahead of the final matchday.

Knowing that victory for their rivals could force them into the automatic relegation spot, Poland will be fearing a clash against in-form Sweden, especially after losing three of their last four outings.

However, the hosts will take heart from the fact they are unbeaten on home soil during this group stage, having drawn 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina on September 25, before thrashing Romania 6-0 a week later.

Meanwhile, Graham Potter's Sweden are yet to taste defeat in Group B4, and are set to play League A football next term following an excellent campaign.

The Blue and Yellow held on to beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-2 on Saturday, racing into a three-goal lead courtesy of a fifth-minute opener from Borussia Dortmund's Daniel Svensson and a pair of penalties from Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres, but conceded twice in a tense second half.

That performance fits Sweden's pattern, considering they have scored in the first 20 minutes during six of their last seven Nations League clashes, while 13 of their past 15 matches have seen both sides find the back of the net.

Regardless, securing their fourth win in five games has Potter's men top of the group with 13 points, five clear of the second-placed Dragons and nine above third-placed Poland.

The Blue and Yellow may no longer be under pressure, but they will be keen to end on a positive note, and having won eight of their last nine meetings with Poland, supporters will be looking forward to another triumph on Tuesday.

Poland will be without Porto centre-back Jakub Kiwior, who is suspended due to accumulating yellow cards, while Aston Villa right-back Matty Cash is a doubt with a leg problem and goalkeeper Kamil Grabara is sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

In their absence, Kacper Potulski could be joined by Tomasz Kedziora at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Arkadiusz Pyrka and Oskar Kubiak at full-back in front of shot-stopper Bartlomiej Dragowski.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan midfielder Piotr Zielinski is unavailable due to illness, though Sebastian Szymanski and Wiktor Nowak should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

As for Sweden, they are missing Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall (knee) and Lech Poznan winger Patrik Walemark (muscle).

With that in mind, expect to see Fulham's Hugo Larsson and Brighton and Hove Albion's Yasin Ayari line up in midfield, while Anthony Elanga and Sebastian Nanasi provide width.

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak will partner Viktor Gyokeres up top on Tuesday, with the latter hoping to add to his brace from last time out.

Dragowski; Pyrka, Potulski, Kedziora, Kubiak; Regula, Szymanski, Nowak, Zalewski; Lewandowski, Swiderski

Johansson; Svensson, Lagerbielke, Lindelof, Gudmundsson; Elanga, Larsson, Ayari, Nanasi; Gyokeres, Isak

Poland are sure to be feeling the pressure from Romania on Tuesday, and they will be keen to confirm their place in the playoffs.

However, Sweden have dominated the head-to-head clashes between these nations, and are likely to continue that trend in midweek.

#1555. Bosnia-Herzegovina vs Romania - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 02:26

Romania will be battling for a chance at avoiding relegation from UEFA Nations League B on Tuesday, when they travel to face Bosnia-Herzegovina at Stadion Bilino Polje.

The Dragons have already secured second in Group B4, and are up against a Tricolorii team that need to win.

Sergej Barbarez's Bosnia-Herzegovina will be hoping to end their group stage on a high note after nailing down a spot in the League A/B playoffs.

The Dragons were downed 3-2 by group winners Sweden on Saturday, conceding three first-half goals before falling agonisingly short of a comeback with two strikes of their own in the second period.

In fairness to Barbarez's side, that loss was their first of this Nations League campaign following two draws and two wins, including a 4-2 triumph over Tuesday's opponents on September 28.

Heading into this clash, Bosnia-Herzegovina are second with eight points - five behind Sweden but four clear of third-placed Poland - and securing the runners-up spot has presented the Dragons with a shot at promotion to League A.

Another victory in midweek could give the team a boost ahead of their playoff, and fans will be expecting a positive result, given that Barbarez's men have not suffered back-to-back defeats since November 2024.

Meanwhile, Gheorghe Hagi's Romania have delivered a dire campaign so far, but escaping with all three points on Saturday has given them a glimmer of hope.

The Tricolorii lost each of their first four Nations League fixtures this term, conceding 13 goals while scoring just three in the process, and seemed doomed to relegation to League C.

However, a shock 2-1 victory over Poland last time out has placed Group B4's bottom side just one point behind the third-placed Eagles in the League B/C playoff spot.

Due to their 6-0 thrashing by Poland on October 2, Romania must beat Bosnia-Herzegovina while hoping that their rivals drop points to Sweden in order to avoid automatic demotion.

That being said, the Tricolorii have not come out on top in any of their eight away matches since hammering San Marino 5-1 in March 2025, losing six times and drawing twice.

Bosnia-Herzegovina have doubts about the readiness of striker Haris Tabakovic, who was forced off just 39 minutes into the clash against Sweden due to a knee injury.

If the Red Bull Salzburg man is unavailable, then Ermedin Demirovic could be joined by Ermin Mahmic up front on Tuesday, supported from out wide by Esmir Bajraktarevic and Kerim Alajbegovic.

At the opposite end of the pitch, centre-back Dennis Hadzikadunic is sidelined with a muscle injury, so Nikola Katic and Stjepan Radeljic should start at the heart of Barbarez's defence.

As for Romania, they are missing midfielder Tudor Baluta, who is suspended for accumulating yellow cards, so Alexandru Cicaldau, Vladimir Screciu and Vlad Dragomir are likely to operate in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Florinel Coman and Dennis Man look set to lead the line once again on Tuesday, aided in attack by Alanyaspor's Ianis Hagi.

Bosnia-Herzegovina possible starting lineup:

Zlomislic; Dedic, Katic, Radeljic, Kolasinac; Bajraktarevic, Basic, Gigovic, Alajbegovic; Mahmic, Demirovic

Hindrich; Ratiu, Coubis, Dragusin, Eissat; Cicaldau, Screciu, Dragomir; Hagi; Coman, Man

Bosnia-Herzegovina may have lost to Sweden at the weekend, but they have proven resilient across this Nations League campaign and will be seen as overwhelming favourites on Tuesday.

Romania have struggled in League B, and given their dire away form - not to mention their four defeats this term - it would be surprising to see the visitors avoid another loss.

#1553. Rio Ferdinand labels Man United's Michael Carrick sacking 'like ChatGPT' - with 142-word statement sent by communications department and no message from club chiefs

Published: 07:20 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:22 EST, 12 November 2026

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand has called for 'a face' to explain the decision to sack Michael Carrick after comparing the club's statement announcing his dismissal to ChatGPT.

Carrick's dismissal was confirmed in a 142-word statement released at 10.37am, which was sent out by Man United's communications department.

Man United have moved closer to appointing former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Man United's key decision makers, including chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, have not issued a message following the decision to part ways with Carrick.

Ferdinand, who played alongside Carrick at Man United, has called for officials to front up to the decision in a post on social media.

'Man United statement like Chat GPT… I wanna hear a voice!' Ferdinand wrote. 'I want to see a face to this…'

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season

Man United's leadership, including minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, were not named in the club's statement

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand called for 'a face' to speak about the decision after comparing the club's statement to ChatGPT

Man United's club statement confirming the decision read: 'Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

'Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

'The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.'

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, Berrada and Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager

Ferdinand, speaking on Rio Presents, claimed Carrick had been disrespected in the way his dismissal had been handled.

'You do everything you can to make this end in the most amicable and respectful and pleasant way possible,' Ferdinand said.

'I think the way it has been done, it could have been done better. I think the leaks coming out of the club are terrible, they don't reflect well on anybody at all.

'It adds to the disrespect to the person in charge at the time. It is terrible to play out in the public like this. The minimum you should get is a bit of respect.'

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins – 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager – six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

#1551. Chile vs Colombia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 16 Nov 2026 04:16

Fresh off the first of two consecutive meetings on Saturday, Chile and Colombia will meet for another international friendly and their final games of 2026 on Tuesday in Santiago.

Tuesday's hosts won the reverse fixture 1-0 away from home, extending their unbeaten streak against Chile.

Chile return to action for their final game of the year on Tuesday aiming to bow out on a positive note after a tough year.

La Roja faced no competitive action in 2026, having fallen short in South American World Cup qualifying last year, meaning they have played just eight times prior to Tuesday's upcoming fixture, losing five and winning three of those.

Nicolas Cordova's team did end the September and October international break with a 2-0 victory over Mexico, thanks to goals from Maximiliano Gutierrez and Vicente Pizarro, but they failed to carry that into the final break of the term, falling short against Colombia again away from home last Saturday.

A trip to Cali ended in a 1-0 loss for La Roja, their fifth defeat in seven games while failing to score for a second time and making it a sixth game against Colombia without a win since a 2019 Copa America penalty shootout triumph.

Now taking their turn to have home advantage for the reverse fixture in Santiago, Chile will set out to end the year with a victory before looking forward and aiming to build in the new year.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip to Santiago aiming to round off their positive year with a double over Chile.

Colombia's 2026 will be remembered for a creditable showing at the World Cup in USA, Mexico and Canada, as La Tricolor topped their group on seven points with two wins and a draw against Portugal.

They would then get past Ghana thanks to Jhon Arias's goal, before falling just short at the hands of Switzerland in the round of 16, losing a penalty shootout after a goalless draw.

In four friendlies since, Nestor Lorenzo's team have won twice, firstly ending the September and October break by beating Peru 2-0 before they beat Chile in Cali on Saturday with a first-half own goal from Guillermo Maripan making the difference.

Now on seven wins in 13 games in the calendar year, Colombia head to Chile looking to make it a perfect final break of 2026 and record another victory.

Nicolas Cordova has a relatively inexperienced Chile squad for the November friendlies, with defenders Paulo Diaz and Benjamin Kuscevic and Paulo Diaz missing out while key midfielder Marcelino Nunez is also not involved.

Ben Brereton Diaz boasts the most experience in a young attacking unit, with 46 caps and 10 international goals to his name, and he may come in from the outset after a substitute appearance in the last game.

That is after Gutierrez, Gonzalo Tapia and Crystal Palace prospect Dario Osorio started in a front three in Colombia, while Rodrigo Echeverria, one of just four players aged above 30 years old, should continue in midfield alongside Vicente Pizarro.

Colombia have also seen plenty of change in their squad, particularly since the World Cup, with James Rodriguez, Juan Quintero and David Ospina retiring while Juan Cuadrado, Santiago Arias, Yerry Mina, Richard Rios and Jhon Duran are also not involved.

Arguably the most notable omission is injured Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz, leaving La Tricolor light and inexperienced up top.

The line should again be led by Luis Suarez, who has eight goals in 21 caps and 13 in 15 appearances across the Primeira Liga and Champions League for Sporting Lisbon, while a new look squad is headlined by the likes of Daniel Munoz, Davinson Sanchez and Jefferson Lerma.

Vigouroux; Villagra, Maripan, Ulloa; Loyola, Echeverria, Pizarro, Suazo; Osorio, Brereton Diaz, Gutierrez

Vargas; Munoz, Sanchez, Lucumi, Velasquez; Duran, Puerta, Lerma, Perea; Suarez, Arias

Given both sides' relatively limited options at the top end of the pitch, we anticipate another low-scoring encounter on Tuesday and give the edge to the visitors to complete a double over Chile.

For now, Arsenal’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing their attacking options rather than confirming a change is imminent. If Gyökeres’ situation develops and Tresoldi maintains his impressive form, the young striker could become one to watch in Arsenal’s future transfer plans.

#1548. “Being talked about…”: Everton plotting January move for “interesting” England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1547. Mauritania vs Burkina Faso - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 16 Nov 2026 06:06, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 06:12

Mauritania and Burkina Faso are back in action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they go head to head at the Stade Cheikha Ould Boidiya on Tuesday evening.

With just four points between first and third in the Group F standings midway through the qualifiers, both nations know the result here could prove decisive in shaping their qualification ambitions.

Having kicked off their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying journey with much promise, consecutive defeats in their last two outings have seen Mauritania's fortunes take a turn for the worse.

Aboubakary Koita, Mamadou Diallo and Alverca striker Dawda Camara all hit the target to fire Les Mourabitounes to a 3-1 opening-day victory over Central African Republic on September 24, five days before crashing back to earth in a 2-1 loss against Benin.

Aritz Lopez Garai’s side were left red-faced on their return to the qualifiers at the weekend, when they fell to a 1-0 defeat against Burkina Faso in the first of their November double-header at the Stade du 4 Aout, with Moise Kabore netting the winner in the 91st minute to sink the visitors.

Having missed the 2025 AFCON, Mauritania find themselves under pressure for a result heading into Tuesday as they sit third in the Group F standings, behind Benin and Burkina Faso, who sit tied on seven points in the first two places.

As for Burkina Faso, head coach Amir Abdou will be pleased with his side’s display on Friday, particularly as it represents a positive response to their crushing 7-0 friendly defeat at the hands of three-time World Champions Argentina in their previous outing on October 4.

The Stallions are now closing on a third straight competitive victory since October 2024, after kicking off their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 1-1 stalemate against Benin in Ouagadougou on September 25, three days before securing a 1-0 win over Central African Republic thanks to a 60th-minute strike from Salzburg striker Aboubacar Camara.

Burkina Faso, who sit 62nd in the latest FIFA World Rankings, are aiming to secure a fourth consecutive AFCON appearance, having finished fourth in 2021 before consecutive round-of-16 exits in 2023 and 2025 respectively.

Abdou’s men will be backing themselves to take pole position in Group F on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have failed to win 10 of the previous 12 meetings between the two nations, losing seven and claiming three draws since May 1987.

Burkina Faso Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

JS Kabylie defender Aly Abeid was forced off injured midway through the game against Burkina Faso at the weekend, and the 28-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday's tie.

In his absence, Olympique Akbou full-back Khadim Diaw should come into the fold, forming the back four with Ibrahima Keita, Mohamed Ali Diadie and Angers’ man Jordan Lefort.

At the attacking end of the pitch, we expect to see an unchanged front three of Abdoullah Ba, Djeidi Gassama and 26-year-old striker Ndiaga Yade, with ZED FC midfielder Maata Magassa retaining his role at the centre of the park.

Off the back of another solid defensive display, we expect Burkina Faso to name an unchanged back four on Tuesday, with Mamoutou Ouedraogo, Nasser Djiga, Edmond Tapsoba and Arsene Kouassi shielding skipper Herve Koffi between the sticks.

Kabore turned in an eye-catching display to hand the Stallions all three points against Mauritania last time out, and the teenage striker could be rewarded with a starting role here, with Lassina Traore, who has failed to find the back of the net in nine games for club and country since September, swearing over his role in the XI.

Diop; Keita, Diadie, Lefort, Diaw; Magassa, Bodda, Gassama; Ba, Koita, Yade

While Mauritania have shown flashes of brilliance in the qualifiers, they find themselves on the cusp of a damaging third consecutive defeat and will be keen to rise to the occasion on Tuesday.

However, Burkina Faso boast superior quality and experience in their rank — particularly at the defensive end of the pitch — and we expect the difference in individual quality to be a decisive factor here, with the Stallions claiming another narrow victory.

#1545. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

[Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he shows a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

"That one was for you, nan" Jack Rudoni explains his goal celebration ❤️ https://t.co/79OvHMlu6J

A victory to savour for Coventry whose teenagers Cherif and Mfuni scored fine goals. No doubt they wobbled when Botman equalised and for the next 10 minutes but Newcastle blew too many chances and resumed making errors at the back. Newcastle’s squad is a mess.

Newcastle might maintain that Thomas-Asante was offside and blocking the keeper’s view when Mfuni pulled the trigger but I think Hornicke had a clear view and hence it wasn’t an offence.

The first two minutes of stoppage time, of which there are four, pass without incident.

Osula lifts a volley over the bar with a wild attempt. Toure was injured in the build-up and will be replaced by Dan Burn.

Never mind Bob Gelodof and Brenda Ann Spencer, Matthias Jaissle doesn’t like Mondays. They are 8-2 down on Monday Night Football so far this season.

Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 (Mfuni) The substitute had only just replaced Rudoni and took the ball on the inside-left 25 yards out, advanced then wrapped his instep around a left-foot shot, arrowing it across Hornicek into the bottom right.

Stephen Mfuni makes his mark for Coventry! 👊 https://t.co/KI2kgpfUJP

Thomas-Asante crashes a right-foot shot into the heart of the left post. A thumping strike that leaves the metalwork ringing.

Coventry 3 Newcastle 1 (Simms) Right foot shot from 18 yards through Thiaw’s legs, clipping the inside of his right knee to deflect it into the bottom left. Joelinton had been trying to dribble it out of the box, overhit it and fouled Thomas-Asante as he tried to recover. The whistle was betweeen the ref’s lips but he did not exhale as Simms steered his shot through Thiaw’s legs.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

Touré beats Dasilva for pace down the right then blazes over from a tight angle then moments later is given an opportunity to shoot and sticks it in the stands again. Both times the cross was on.

Toure has caused untold problems for Dasilva. Newcastle corner on the left is bent far too deep and goes out for a goal-kick.

Wissa dithers over a shot when found by Toure to the right of the penalty spot and finally clips it into Thomas. Coventry are clinging on but flapping. As is the crowd.

Hall, following Botman’s lead, lets fly from distance, straight at Rushworth.

Coventry fluff a couple of chances to break with hasty, panicked passes.

It was as if Coventry were defying him to have a shot. And in doing so, the nerves are back with a bang in the crowd.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 1 (Botman) Coventry invite him to shoot by backing off and backing off and he RSVPs with a left-foot torpedo from 20 yards into the roof of the net. What a strike!

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

Barnes appears to have been brought down by Sakamoto in the Coventry penalty area but he was offside. One of Jaissle’s staff is booked for some verbal transgression.

Joelinto rattles bones in a tackle that was not shown as they focus on Barnes’ spurious penalty appeal when he slipped behind Pinnock.

Rudoni dips his shoulder and skins Botman in the Newcastle box but tries and fails to square it to Cherif instead of shooting.

Touré makes ground down the right and slips Joelinton down the inside. The substitute, who took the captain’s armband off Thiaw, tries to find Pardo with a cross that Thomas blocks.

Now Willock blazes over from eight yards on the right after a slick one-two with Murphy.

Dedic → MileyTouré → MurphyJoelinton → Willock

Rushworth drops Hall’s cross but recovers to grab it on the bounce. Jaissle has three subs stripped. Murphy tries to bend a cross from the right to Barnes at the back post but Van Ewijk and Thomas combine to scramble it out for a throw-in.

Now Cherif misses a gilded opportunity after a hacked clearance from Botman lands at his feet to the left of the spot. He kicks it into his other leg and the ball dribbles wide. The way Botman dealt with Thomas-Asante’s cross was really shoddy.

Barnes disguises his inside run and evades Van Ewijk to collect Thiaw’s pass up the inside-right channel. He spins and feeds it infield to Wissa who telegraphs his shot with a laboured touch before swiinging a right-footer from 25 yards straight down Rushworth’s throat.

Newcastle have been awful. Seem to lack leadership and heft on the field. The return of Joelinton can’t come quick enough.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 0 (Cherif) Talented lad. Absolutely larrups a right-foot shot through a thicket of Newcastle legs from 18 yards when a long throw was headed out to the edge of the box.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

Collison between Van Ewijk and Willock leaves them both winded and needing treatment. The Newcastle midfielder had been trying to bullock down the middle in purusit of a pass.

Coventry overload with seven men on the right before rolling the kick-off to the left-footed Rushworth who launches it too far up that wing and Hornicek gathers.

Interesting half for Matias Fernandez-Pardo who has been in the middle of most of Newcastle’s best moments but has failed to take two excellent chances.

The first was baffling as the Belgium international made no attempt to sweep in Jacob Murphy’s cutback at the near post, letting it run through his legs thinking Harvey Barnes was in a better position. He wasn’t.

The second was a little unfortunate as he did well to time his run and wriggle free of centre back Bobby Thomas. That put him in on goal with just the goalkeeper to beat, but having sat Chris Rushworth down he pushed the ball a fraction too wide and by the time he was in a position to shoot, Thomas had done brilliantly to cut off the angle and block it.

Coventry have been good but Newcastle have been really poor again away from home. They are yet to put a 90-minute performance together since the opening weekend against Liverpool. Matthias Jaissle will want a lot more from his team in the second half.

Newcastle should at least be level given their chances but you have to admire Coventry’s spirit and work rate. Cherif seems to me to have a high ceiling and at 19 is already a real handful.

Newcastle need to stop fannying around and buy a proper centre-forward. Wissa is better wide or in a more fluid system, as I suspect Fernandez-Pardo is, too. Stick Osula on and get the chequebook out in January. Offer Boro £50m for Lankshear.

Cheeif, working his socks off, chases a lost cause and retrieves a long pass forward in the whitewash but when he turns to try to play it to Thomas-Asante, Thiaw makes a good tackle.

Hall turns away Mason-Clark’s effort from the left and the game turns into a basketball match… without the scoring as both sides fly from end to end.  Two minutes of stoppage time to come.

Thomas to the rescue again, He was outpaced by Fernandez-Pardo running on to straight ball down the middle but kept on going when the Belgium forward rounded the keeper to block the shot. Fernandez-Pardo may have been better off taking on the shot earlier, surprising the advancing Rushworth, rather than trying to take him out of the equation. Or dinked it before he got too close.

Newcastle force Coventry all the way back to Rushworth who knocks it long to Dasilva who holds it up well and passes to Mason-Clark. The left-winger runs and then tries to force the ball through Thiaw instead of laying it back to the left-back who was free. Thiaw makes the block.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.
