#1543. Man City: Why the international break could be vital for Maresca

By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 06:59

Manchester City began the season with the impression that adapting to Enzo Maresca’s work would be quick. With seven wins in the opening Premier League rounds, the team took the lead and at one point opened up a six-point advantage over Arsenal. The run, however, was abruptly interrupted.

Defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest dropped the team to third place and allowed the current champions to pull clear at the top.

More than the scorelines, the performances exposed difficulties in competing physically, winning duels and protecting the defence when possession is lost. Maresca himself acknowledged that his team could not keep up with the intensity of the opposition in the first half.

So the November international break comes at a good time. The pause will not erase the problems that have appeared in recent weeks, nor does it mean that all the players will have days off. But it offers the manager a valuable opportunity to assess performance, recover players and work on adjustments that would hardly be possible with a run of matches.

The drop in City’s level cannot be explained only by a lack of efficiency in front of goal.

The team can still control possession and produce offensive volume. Against Forest, for example, it finished the game with 79 per cent possession and 12 shots. The problem is that this control has not been enough to stop opponents finding space and creating dangerous situations.

One of the main issues is defensive protection. City have conceded 17 goals in eight matches and have not kept a clean sheet in any of their last nine games. The high defensive line, a hallmark of Maresca’s teams, demands coordination between the units and a quick ability to react to losing the ball. When the counter-press does not work, the defenders are left exposed to fast attacks and have to defend large spaces.

The absence of Rodri helps to explain part of this difficulty. The Spaniard offered reading of the game, interceptions and the quality to organise the build-up. More than a defensive midfielder who protects the defence, he is a player capable of anticipating danger and stopping counter-attacks before they gather speed. Without him, the rest of the midfield has to share responsibilities that Rodri used to take on almost alone.

Elliot Anderson has been important in this context, but so too is the distribution of roles. The presence of players such as Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki adds technical quality and creativity, but also demands defensive cover. If the two play together without a structure that protects the central area, Anderson can be overburdened in covering and in physical duels.

The break allows Maresca to work on these relationships. One possibility is to adjust the make-up of the midfield, ensuring more balance between creation and protection. Another is to review the team’s positioning without the ball, especially the distance between the defensive line and the most advanced players. It is not necessarily a question of abandoning the style of play, but of finding ways to make it less vulnerable.

The calendar and the physical condition of the squad are another important aspect. City lost rhythm during a demanding period of fixtures, and the recovery of players can help the team regain the intensity needed to execute Maresca’s model.

It will also be important to monitor the situation of Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. Both were substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because of physical problems, according to Maresca. The break could be useful to assess the extent of the issues and avoid important players returning before they are fully fit.

There is, however, a caveat: the international break is not a holiday for the whole squad. Several starters have been called up by their national teams, among them Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Gvardiol, Guehi, Enzo Fernandez and Cherki. Travel and international commitments reduce the recovery time for some players, while others will be able to stay in Manchester and work directly with the coaching staff.

Even so, the break offers an opportunity to reorganise the workload and prepare the squad for what follows. In a season in which intensity is essential to the functioning of Maresca’s system, managing physical wear and tear is also part of the recovery process.

The break arrives at a time when City need to recover not only results, but also confidence in their own way of playing. The seven opening wins showed that the team has the resources to compete for the title. The three defeats that followed, on the other hand, revealed that there are still important adjustments to be made to sustain that level over an entire season.

The first challenge after the break will be against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. Then the team will face an even more significant fixture: the visit to Arsenal on 29 November. The six-point gap makes the direct meeting an important opportunity to close the distance, although the result will not be enough, by itself, to settle the title race.

For Maresca, the international break is a chance to find answers before the run of negative results turns into an even bigger problem. The manager needs to restore defensive solidity, find the best distribution of roles in midfield and make possession dominance translate into effective control of matches again.

City do not need to abandon their identity to react. Above all, they need to find a better balance between what they do with the ball and what they can do when they lose it. If the break allows Maresca to progress with this work and recover important players, the team could return better prepared to face a decisive stretch of the season.

#1542. Michael Carrick is SACKED by Man United: Manager leaves training ground just 2½ hours after arriving - and now Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over

Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026

Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.

Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

In a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick have indicated. They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season

Carrick was seen leaving the training ground less than two and a half hours later

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday morning after it had emerged that Berrada and Wilcox were heading to Monaco to recommend his sacking and did so again on Wednesday when it transpired United were closing in on an agreement to bring in Pochettino as his successor.

The current United States national team manager reached a verbal agreement with Man United to take over on Wednesday. United then made a formal approach to US Soccer shortly after, with the club having to trigger the 54-year-old Argentine's £7million release clause.

The final nail in Carrick’s coffin came in Sunday's dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which saw United stuck in the relegation zone in 18th position.

The handling of Carrick’s departure has been particularly damning on Ineos and the shot-callers at United, not least given he was given no show of public support when he continued in post following an emergency board meeting after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

A defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez badly let his manager down by getting sent off, and a win over Roma to go with the draw against Villa, was not enough of a sign that it will turn around for the board to keep faith.

With Carrick's departure, it pushes the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million. Buying Pochettino out of his contract with the US national team will cost another £7m. Adding his large coaching staff will take millions more.

Matchgoing supporters will be sad to see Carrick go and made those feelings clear in recent games when he was loudly cheered at the end of matches, with the ire and frustration levelled against players and executives.

Optimism heading into the campaign was sky high given that no team in the Premier League performed better than Carrick's side between January and May.

But that level of success and dominance has long since evaporated after a shambolic start to the current campaign - and it has cost the 45-year-old his job just five months after the ink dried on a new deal.

It has been a season in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league all season.

A season in which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned his manager's tactics and Martinez eviscerated the hierarchy for hanging Carrick and the players out to dry. Fernandes was even dropped for the first time in five years for the Bournemouth humiliation.

Questions will continue to be asked of those upstairs, with Berrada and Wilcox now on to their third permanent manager this year alone and their fourth in their tenure having burned through Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick since taking control of football operations in February 2024.

It means Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (pictured on Thursday morning) need a third manager this year as INEOS' running of the football club comes under scrutiny once more

Sunday's draw with Aston Villa proved to be the final nail in the coffin for the United boss

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players

Amorim lasted 14 months in the role, even in spite of embarrassing defeats to the likes of League Two Grimsby Town, but for Carrick it was a dream job that would run until early November and end in him being unceremoniously dumped at the training ground by Wilcox.

Carrick vowed after the Villa draw that he wouldn’t walk away and took on a spiky side when quizzed on his future by reporters. After a week of shame against the board, he has finally been put out of his misery.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins - 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager - six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Now it looks set to be Pochettino’s challenge to turn this massively underperforming squad around, something former United star Gary Neville believes is a mightily difficult task given the 'unprofessional' squad the new man will inherit.

'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned [Carrick] for a few months. They have, they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast recently.

'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though.

'He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.

'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

#1533. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage after disastrous 16-game spell - this is how his reign unravelled over late, intense sessions, dinner at the training ground and an unpopular assistant manager

Published: 10:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:52 EST, 12 November 2026

Crystal Palace have sacked Pierre Sage after players and club chiefs grew frustrated over his training methods, Daily Mail Sport can reveal.

A 3-1 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday saw Palace drop to bottom of the Premier League for the first time in nine years and proved to be the final straw for club bosses.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while the Palace players got on well with the 47-year-old, they were frustrated by his late training sessions – with some not starting until 4pm. The regimented routine required players to stay at the training ground for dinner on the night before matches, with some not returning home until 8pm ahead of a 2pm kick-off the following day.

The club's hierarchy, meanwhile, expressed concerns early in the Frenchman's tenure that he was not doing enough defensive work on the training pitch.

Sage's philosophy was that the best way to defend was having the ball, meaning training sessions focused on running, pressing and possession rather than defensive structure.

But the lack of focus led to a poor defensive record, with Palace conceding 30 goals in 16 matches across all competitions. Defending set-pieces and counter-attacks has been a persistent problem for Sage’s side, and he won just two of his ten Premier League games in charge.

Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace after a dismal start to the season saw them win just two of their first ten games

Palace sit rock bottom of the Premier League, their leaky defence having conceded 24 goals

Daily Mail Sport understands many players voiced fears they were being pushed too hard in training, with sessions the day before a game particularly intense. There were also significant concerns about the quality of Sage's backroom staff, with his assistant Jamal Alioui proving especially unpopular among the players.

There has also been considerable turnover among senior executives, with six departures over the past 18 months. Chief financial officer Mitesh Velani is set to add to that number in the coming months. One well-placed source told Daily Mail Sport that the disruption to the club’s business operations has the hallmarks of a club heading for relegation.

As Palace look to bail themselves out of trouble, Daily Mail Sport understands talks are progressing with former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank, who is expected to take over ahead of crucial games against Coventry and Hull after the international break.

Palace chairman Steve Parish first contemplated sacking Sage over his lack of defensive nous in September, but gave him a stay of execution after Palace kept a clean sheet in a spirited performance away at Leeds on the eve of the international break. However, that display proved an anomaly as Palace shipped 19 goals in the following nine games.

Palace have won just once in their last eight matches in all competitions, beating Fulham 1-0 in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

In September, Daily Mail Sport revealed tensions had emerged between Sage and Parish when the latter took a dim view of the decision to drop teenage defender Jaydee Canvot for their defeat by Ipswich Town.

Palace paid French club RC Lens £4million in compensation to appoint Sage in June after he won the French Cup, finished second in Ligue 1 behind Paris Saint-Germain and was named manager of the season last term. It was the first time in 10 years that Palace had paid compensation to appoint a manager.

Palace chairman Steve Parish (right) first contemplated dismissing Sage in September over a lack of defensive nous

Palace players found Sage’s training sessions too intense and struggled to adapt to the late schedule

Succeeding Oliver Glasner, Palace's greatest manager, proved too big a task for Sage.

Following Palace's loss to Liverpool, Sage insisted the Eagles have been playing better than their league position suggests and pleaded for more time. Those appeals fell on deaf ears.

'A lot of times I’ve said we deserved better and it was the case again (on Sunday),' said Sage. 'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

‘I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in (me), and if it's not the case, they will take a decision. I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100 per cent involved in what I have to do.

‘We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be OK.’

#1529. Mirabelli reminisces on Calhanoglu signing and Milan disappointment: “A bitter taste”

Today, Massimiliano Mirabelli has looked back on his time at AC Milan and his favourite signing from his short time with the club.

After arriving before the 2017 summer transfer window, there was hope that Mirabelli would oversee a new era with Milan. However, he never got given the extended period to oversee that change that he’d hoped for.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Indeed, just a year later, the Elliott fund arrived and he was removed from his role as the Rossoneri truly entered a new era.

Responsible for the signings of Andre Silva, Andrea Conti and most notably Leonardo Bonucci, you wonder what would’ve happened if he’d stayed with the Rossoneri for longer. Nevertheless, with what and who eventually arrived, there’s no point considering the alternative, especially given he took a four-year break after his time with the club.

Speaking to Tuttosport, via MilanNews, Mirabelli spoke about the disappointment of his time with the Rossoneri and his pride in bringing Hakan Calhanoglu to Italy.

“Unfortunately, the experience in Milan was short-lived due to the change of ownership. It left a bitter taste in our mouths because we weren’t given the opportunity to complete a long-term project.

“Roma wasn’t built in a day… The deal that still makes me proud today? The Calhanoglu deal . Without a doubt, the best and most successful gamble of my career. We’re talking about the man who, for me, remains the most complete midfielder in Europe to this day. He has incredible, uncommon qualities.

“I started following him when I worked at Inter. We couldn’t sign him from Leverkusen due to an ongoing lawsuit over his double registration as a minor, which resulted in his suspension.

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“The biggest discussion, then, was about his position. We spent hours with Montella and—later—with Gattuso to understand where he could best express himself. At Leverkusen, he’d played everywhere: as a midfielder, as an attacking midfielder, and even as a winger.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

#1528. Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi criticised by Spanish media after being "overwhelmed" in Spain 2-3 England

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 09:32, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 09:38

England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run in all competitions courtesy of a 3-2 success in Madrid in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday night.

An extraordinary match saw England lead 3-0 before Spain attempted to launch a fightback, but the Three Lions held on to secure all three points.

The result has allowed England to top Group 3 of League A in the Nations League.

Spain have joined Thomas Tuchel's side in the quarter-finals of the tournament, but their long unbeaten run has now come to an end.

Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi was handed another start in the middle of the Spain midfield, but it proved to be a difficult night for the 27-year-old, who played in a protective mark due to a broken nose that he suffered while playing for the Gunners last month.

Zubimendi was substituted in the 72nd minute due to an apparent injury, and it remains to be seen whether he is now facing a period on the sidelines.

El Desmarque were especially critical of Zubimendi, saying that the midfielder was simply "overwhelmed" by England, who adopted a high-press from the very first whistle.

AS also detailed Zubimendi's issues, with the publication noting his struggles to dictate the play against Gunners teammate Declan Rice, while his use of the ball was also criticised.

Mundo Deportivo said that the midfielder was "exhausted" due to England's press, with Zubimendi hardly ever given time to settle on the ball.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult start to the season for Zubimendi, and there has recently been speculation surrounding his future.

The midfielder has played 12 times for the Gunners this term, but he has not made a single start in the Premier League, with his seven outings - totalling 101 minutes - coming from the bench, while he has played just 98 minutes of Champions League football this term.

Zubimendi is not currently first choice in the Arsenal midfield, and his lack of football this season could have contributed to his struggles against England, as the 27-year-old did appear to lack sharpness in the Nations League fixture.

It remains to be seen whether the Spaniard stays at Arsenal on a long-term basis, but it is believed that a number of La Liga clubs are keen to bring him back to the division next year.

#1527. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1526. Unai Emery's grand plans for Aston Villa after agreeing new contract: Why he believes he can win Champions League, the Pep Guardiola blueprint and changing his mind on selling stars

Published: 07:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:54 EST, 12 November 2026

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson but when planning the current stage of his career the Spaniard had another boss in mind.

Having agreed a new contract that will make him one of the two best paid managers in the Premier League, Emery has the sort of structure at Villa that Pep Guardiola enjoyed for a decade at Manchester City.

Emery has always regarded Guardiola as the world’s best coach – and not just for the teams he has produced and the trophies he has won. The Basque admired Guardiola’s refusal to compromise on his vision for a club and has adopted those principles every step of the way at Villa, leading them from the bottom half to the Champions League.

‘We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a (new) deal, yes,’ Emery said last Friday, of a meeting he had with key figures at Villa including co-owner Nassef Sawiris a few days earlier. ‘Nassef is very ambitious, a hard worker and his commitment to the club is huge. It’s easy for me to have meetings with him as normally we are on the same page.’

This season began slowly but after six league games unbeaten, Villa are back in the top half and three points off the top five, as well as sitting sixth in the Champions League group phase with three wins from four.

After Emery underlined his desire to stay at Villa Park, Daily Mail Sport looks at what comes next for him and Villa.

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares to extend his stay in the Midlands

After a slow start this season, Villa are in fine form in both the Premier League and Champions League

With about two-and-a-half years still remaining on Emery’s previous deal, there was no need for Sawiris to rush. His decision is both a show of faith and a recognition of the current climate.

Emery was on a five-man shortlist to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United but Daily Mail Sport understands he is unlikely to have moved to Old Trafford even without the contract discussions.

Studying Guardiola convinced Emery that to be successful, a manager needs control. He cannot operate if he has only limited influence over recruitment, or if he has no say in senior appointments – something United are highly unlikely to have granted.

Unlike at many clubs, where sporting directors and heads of performance are brought in by the chairman or chief executive, Emery has driven the key hires at Villa. Since Emery’s arrival, the number of Spanish backroom staff at Villa has grown well into double figures.

Director of football operations Damian Vidagany moved to Villa with Emery in 2022 and was a key reason why Emery accepted the job. Emery also pushed for Monchi to be brought in as ‘president of football operations’ and when that went wrong, he was allowed to select the next guy – Roberto Olabe. It is hard to imagine many other clubs where that would happen.

So far Olabe has been much better than his predecessor, whose dire record in the market saw him ditched a little more than a year ago.

Emery would have had none of this influence at United. In Sawiris, he has a highly supportive boss – contrast that with Sir Jim Ratcliffe. He makes the final calls on recruitment, rather than relying on the equivalent of Jason Wilcox.

Emery’s sense of self-worth is too great and his record too impressive to accept answering to executives of inferior ability. At Villa, he answers only to the ownership group, and he has forged a rock-solid relationship with Sawiris.

Emery was the driving force behind the appointments of director of football operations Damian Vidagany (left) and president of football operations Roberto Olabe (right)

Emery has a rock-solid relationship with co-owner Nassef Sawiris

There are few top clubs these days where the manager has a direct line to the owner but the Sawiris-Emery connection took shape in the autumn of 2022, weeks before he was hired. Sawiris could see the Steven Gerrard experiment was failing and wanted a top-class manager. He looked at Mauricio Pochettino, Thomas Tuchel and Emery.

After a difficult experience at Arsenal, Emery had won the Europa League with Villarreal and was assured by Sawiris that he would have the run of Villa. Emery felt he had never had this level of influence during his 18 months at Arsenal and throughout the process, Sawiris has been as good as his word.

Emery joined on just under £10million per year and his new salary would be close to double that. His wishes in the market have been backed, even when it has been tricky to make the sums add up. Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in January 2025 to deliver Champions League football. That did not happen, but there was no blowback for Emery because Sawiris trusted the direction of travel.

Every one of his requests has been approved. The current stadium redevelopment was planned for 2024 but was shelved because Emery did not wish to play Champions League games in a three-sided ground. Now, he has accepted the bigger picture.

At the training ground, a 40-room hotel was signed off on Emery’s say-so. When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi who took the rap, not Emery.

That sort of loyalty cuts both ways. With their stock so high, how many managers would have stuck around after six of their first-choice starting XI from a Europa League final win had been sold? Emery is taking a risk to his reputation by leading this rebuild but he trusts both himself and Sawiris to get it right.

Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in 2025 to deliver Champions League football. There was no blowback for Emery when that did not happen

When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi (pictured) who took the rap, not Emery

There was a moment at the end of Friday’s press conference when Emery showed just how much he was invested in Aston Villa.

The Spaniard had just been asked if he could elevate Villa to the same level as Europe’s giants and instead of delivering the usual platitudes, Emery referred to the Deloitte Money League, which ranks clubs by the revenue they generate.

To emphasise his point, Emery grabbed his phone, found the page and confirmed that Villa had risen to 14th in the 2024-25 list, generating £376m in that period.

How many top-flight managers are even aware of the Deloitte Money League, let alone their club’s position in it? When asked about finances, most bosses will – quite legitimately – answer that these matters are for senior executives to handle.

Not Emery, who has made a definite shift in recent seasons. He now understands that because of Villa’s financial needs, part of his job will be to sign promising players, increase their value and then – potentially – sell them for double the fee.

This summer, Villa sold Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Ollie Watkins for a combined £253m. They were signed for a total of just £48m.

You can already picture Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi, two of the summer additions, falling into this category.

The unknown is how Emery might feel about this strategy in two or three years’ time if Villa slip out of contention for the Champions League.

Because for all the justifiable enthusiasm about a new contract, this will not be an easy road. Not surprisingly for an overhauled team, Villa are inconsistent.

Villa bought Morgan Rogers (fourth left), Ollie Watkins (fourth right), Ezri Konsa (right) and Youri Tielemans (not pictured) for a combined £48m, then sold them all this summer for £253m

You can already see Johan Manzambi - signed for £52m this summer - being the next player Villa make a huge profit from

After the Europa League triumph in May, Emery's dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa

Throw in their issues with financial regulations and the stadium rebuild and it would be no shock – nor any disgrace – if they finished outside the top five for the next couple of seasons.

Would that be enough for Emery, though? His dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa.

Emery cited Leicester winning the Premier League and his own journey with Villarreal to the Champions League semi-finals in 2022.

Yet the rules are stacked in favour of the wealthiest and no matter how hard they try, Villa may never crack the code. By investing so heavily in Emery, though, Sawiris believes he is giving them a proper shot.

#1523. Jurgen Klopp calls for Gianni Infantino to be replaced as FIFA president – ‘Worse than Sepp Blatter’

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 09:47, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 09:48

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA leadership as he believes that president Gianni Infantino is worse than disgraced predecessor Sepp Blatter.

Infantino has spent the last 10 years in the most powerful position in global football and has frequently faced criticism, but widespread backlash aimed at the 56-year-old Swiss chief has grown since the 2026 World Cup.

In the summer, Infantino came under fire for his involvement in overturning a red card suspension for USA striker Folarin Balogun following a phone call from U.S. President Donald Trump.

Infantino's position at FIFA was plunged into a deeper crisis when he announced controversial plans to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

This attracted major opposition from several football confederations including UEFA, who threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments, but the ‘FIFA Forward Enterprises’ has since been scrapped.

Infantino became FIFA president in 2016 after former chief Blatter stepped down amid a ​major corruption scandal that lead to him facing criminal charges.

Infantino was then re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023, and intends to stand again for a fourth term in March, but Klopp is one high-profile figure keen for change at the very top of football.

Indeed, the Germany boss made his feelings clear on Infantino during a press conference ahead of Germany’s UEFA Nations League showdown with the Netherlands on Monday.

“The general consensus is that a change might make sense,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters.

“After Sepp Blatter, we thought things couldn’t get any worse, and then we managed to pull it off.

“There are certainly people who care about football and have no financial interests. If one of them were to take over, it would be absolutely helpful.”

While working as a pundit before taking the Germany job earlier this year, Klopp slammed the decision for Balogun’s red card to be overturned at the World Cup, and was particularly critical of Trump’s apparent involvement.

“If that really was the case, then that’s crazy,” Klopp said in July. “Let’s just say: this is our game, not theirs.

“These two people (Trump and Infantino), who both have no idea about football, should have nothing to do with that. That was a red card. There’s no two ways about it.”

Klopp was appointed Germany head coach a few weeks later, replacing Julian Nagelsmann following the country’s shock last-32 exit on penalties to Paraguay at the World Cup.

The 59-year-old has not publicly stated who he would like to see take the FIFA presidency from Infantino, but former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega and Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to challenge him.

Meanwhile, former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Infantino as a candidate in FIFA’s presidential election, despite allegedly receiving backing from France president Emmanuel Macron.

Wenger - who had distanced himself from Infantino’s aborted FIFA Forward Enterprises plan - currently holds the role of Head of Global Development at FIFA and is expected to continue in this position.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

“I think it was a tough match. They studied our team well, and even the details ultimately fell in their favour. Then we ended up losing momentum a bit, but that’s something that happens and is part of it.

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

Mauricio Pochettino has been warned against taking the Manchester United job, by Gary Neville unless the club's hierarchy promise to back him in the January transfer window and bolster 'the worst back four in the Premier League'.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Pochettino is expected to be named as the new Red Devils head coach, replacing Michael Carrick. Carrick was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning before being sacked just hours later.

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning too. He had been in Monaco the day before with the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Upon Pochettino's expected arrival, he will join a club languishing in the relegation zone - with United 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 matches.

United have conceded 19 goals across those 10 games - with only 14th-placed Ipswich Town (20) and bottom side Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) has been warned against becoming the new Manchester United head coach by Gary Neville unless they promise him defensive reinforcements in January

Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington on Thursday morning ahead of his Man United sacking

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning after being in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's fate at the club

And speaking about Pochettino's pending arrival, Neville insists on the Argentine making ultimatums to the board if they want him - starting with improving the defence.

'If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven,' he said on The Overlap.

'He'll do that with a pay-off. So do that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January. He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer we're not to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

'They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.'

Expanding further, the former United right back didn't hold back in his criticism of the current defensive options at the club.

'I mean look the back four that he finished with on Sunday was [Diogo] Dalot left back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,' he said.

'That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.'

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

Neville believes Manchester United have 'the worst back four in the Premier League'

Diogo Dalot (left) gave away a penalty during United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

#1518. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1513. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

🗣️ "There’s only one way to win games: you have to want it more than your opponents"

The Bianconeri host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Serie A Matchday 10, and coach Luciano Spalletti previewed the action ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/8lyakgqdxW#JuveNapoli pic.twitter.com/KGApOET8on

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 31, 2026

The fixture also brings Spalletti back against Napoli, the club he won the title with. The last meeting, in January 2026 at the Allianz Stadium, ended 3-0 to Juventus. Jonathan David, Kenan Yildiz and Filip Kostić scored. A win on Sunday would lift Juventus clear of a direct rival. Spalletti’s pre-match press conference is set for Saturday 31 October at 17:00, the day before kick-off.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1509. Spalletti calls job question provocative and vows no step back before Napoli

Luciano Spalletti struck a defiant tone on the eve of Juventus-Napoli, a game seen as a must-win. He also backed the club's response to the defeat at Genoa, including a squad retreat.

Spalletti made his stance clear on the eve of Juventus-Napoli. Anyone expecting him to retreat even slightly, he warned, should expect something different.

Sunday’s game is at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti said the side want to win back the respect that has been taken from them. Several outlets say his job is on the line.

The build-up has been shaped by the club’s response to the defeat at Genoa. Ehizibue scored in the 12th minute and Baldanzi in the 28th. After a long meeting between chief executive Giovanni Carnevali and the squad, Spalletti announced a retreat. The team would stay at the Continassa from Friday evening until the Napoli game.

Spalletti called Carnevali’s address perfect and said he had hit the right notes. He has never been keen on training-camp retreats. In these circumstances, though, he said one could help the group become more compact again.

The coach also played down any need for public backing. He needs no reassurance from the club, only a reaction from the team, Eurosport reported. He added that he is not asking his players for anything beyond their capabilities.

After nine rounds, this season’s tally trails the 15 Juventus had at the same stage last season and the 17 under Motta in 2024/25. It is above the 13 under Allegri in 2022/23, according to Tuttosport.

Recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. A 2-0 win at Lecce and the loss at Genoa complete the run. Two of those five games ended in defeat, and Juventus failed to score in both.

Napoli arrive without their coach. The Serie A sporting judge banned Massimiliano Allegri for two matches over disrespectful remarks to the officials in the 3-3 draw with Roma. The ban covers the Monza and Juventus games.

#1507. Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku announces shock retirement from international football

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05

Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has announced that he has retired from international football.

With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.

Lukaku's most recent outing for Belgium was against France on November 5, the 33-year-old donning the captain's armband on that occasion.

However, Lukaku did not play in Belgium's last two fixtures, being ruled out versus Turkey last Thursday due to a hip injury and remaining as an unused substitute for Sunday's 4-1 victory over Italy.

On Monday morning, Lukaku took to social media to make the surprise revelation that he had called time on his international career.

A statement on Instagram read: "Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team…I experienced every emotion imaginable…

"I was lucky enough to play alongside extraordinary teammates, to whom I will always be grateful. I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches who pushed me to give my best and trusted me to help the team. It was a wonderful journey, and I cherished every moment.

"To the Belgian fans, thank you for all the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was incredible. I enjoyed it immensely. I am grateful. Thank you."

Under both Rudi Garcia at the World Cup and Mark van Bommel across the six recent UEFA Nations League matches, Lukaku has not been viewed as a certain starter.

That is despite the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scoring in four of his last seven outings for his country.

While Lukaku has not shed light on any potential issues behind the scenes, an assumption can be made that remaining as an unused substitute in two of the five games that he was available under Van Bommel has played its part.

At the age of 33, Lukaku had the opportunity to join a list of players who have reached 100 goals for their country. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Ali Daei have achieved that feat.

Choosing to stay six goals short of the illustrious three figures feels an unusual choice on Lukaku's part, but it does not take away from ending his international career with 53 goals more than any other Belgian player in history.

#1506. Why Man United decided against appointing Didier Deschamps as their new head coach

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 11:52, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 11:55

Manchester United had reportedly considered Didier Deschamps as a replacement for Michael Carrick, but conversations with the Frenchman and his representatives over a move to Old Trafford 'did not go well'.

Carrick was sacked by Man United last week due to the team's struggles in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been appointed at his replacement, with the Argentine due to officially take charge on November 18.

In the latter stages of Carrick's time at Old Trafford, there were suggestions that Deschamps was being seriously considered as a replacement for the Englishman.

According to The Athletic, contact was made over a potential move for the 58-year-old, who stepped down as France head coach following the 2026 World Cup.

However, the report claims that the conversations 'did not go well'.

Man United allegedly believed that Deschamps was looking to gain leverage for a move to manage in Saudi Arabia.

Deschamps has been in charge of Monaco, Juventus and Marseille during his club management career, while he was France's boss between 2012 and 2026.

The former midfielder guided Monaco to success in the Coupe de la Ligue, in addition to overseeing a spot in the 2003-04 Champions League final.

Deschamps also lifted the Serie B title in 2006-07 while in charge of Juventus, in addition to Ligue 1, three Coupe de la Ligue trophies and two Trophee des Champions while at Marseille.

For France, Deschamps guided the team to the 2018 World Cup and 2020-21 UEFA Nations League trophies, in addition to helping the Blues reach the final of Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup.

Deschamps is thought to be in line for a move to Saudi Arabia at some stage in the near future.

Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were also all linked with the role at Old Trafford before Pochettino's arrival was confirmed.

Pochettino will be aiming to make the perfect start to life at Man United when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League this weekend.

#1505. EFL asks clubs to stop targeted 'banter' on social media amid fears over reputational damage in the wake of 'Spygate' fallout

Published: 09:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EST, 12 November 2026

The EFL has written to clubs calling for a halt in reputationally damaging social media posts disguised as ‘banter’ - believing the line has been blurred when it comes to regulatory matters.

The letter expressed concern over a ‘growing pattern of posts that use disputes, disciplinary matters, alleged wrongdoing or rival Clubs as material for public “banter”.’

A letter, seen by Daily Mail Sport, has been sent by EFL chief executive Trevor Birch to club chairs and executives following a board meeting.

‘While any one post may be viewed as an isolated lapse, taken together they risk creating a culture in which short-term engagement is prioritised over judgement, responsibility and long-term reputation,’ the letter read.

‘This is not about removing humour, personality or rivalry from Club channels. It is about recognising when content becomes disparaging, prolongs a dispute, targets an individual, or calls the integrity of a Club or the competition into question.

‘The impact extends beyond the Clubs directly involved. Repeated public exchanges can inflame relationships, undermine confidence in the fairness and professionalism of our competitions, and weaken the collective EFL brand.

The EFL have called for clubs to halt 'banter' social media posts. Pictured: Wrexham owners Rob Mac (left) and Ryan Reynolds (right) spoofed Southampton's Spygate case in September. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Wrexham were among the clubs to mock the case by putting a not to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors' prior to their match with Southampton on fixture release day. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Birmingham City also referenced the case by revealing the date for their fixture by showing the club badges cut into hedges and visible through binoculars. Source: X/BCFC

‘Recent media interest in perceived public disputes between Clubs illustrates how quickly individual posts can become a wider reputational issue.’

Daily Mail Sport understands the EFL are keen to avoid being seen as killjoys. Rather, they are taking a preventative approach to posts that could end up breaching FA or EFL rules.

The Southampton ‘Spygate’ scandal is among the most prominent disputes that have been referenced by clubs in social media content in recent months.

Both Birmingham City and Wrexham shared posts on the Championship fixture release date in June, using the case to highlight the dates of a fixture with Southampton.

Birmingham’s official X account posted a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into hedges which were viewed through binoculars. The account added: ‘One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on...’

Wrexham’s calendar for their matches in September included a reminder to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors’ two days before they played Southampton. An image of a man behind a tree was included in the Southampton badge.

The club also included their Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac in a spoof video in the build-up to the match. The actors were seen behind a tree similar to one which Southampton intern William Salt was caught spying near ahead of their play-off semi-final with Middlesbrough.

Following the revelations by Daily Mail Sport, Southampton were eventually thrown out of the play-offs.

Last week, Blackburn hit back at a video of West Ham manager Scott Parker declaring he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan’ by showing images of their supporters celebrating goals in their 2-1 win over the Hammers.

Blackburn hit back at West Ham boss Scott Parker last week after he declared he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan', with the club then showing supporters celebrating goals. Source: X/Rovers

The EFL reminded clubs in their letter that regulations called for clubs to ‘to act towards one another with utmost good faith’. The organisation called for clubs to consider whether their content is ‘punching down’ or ‘targeting a specific Club or individual’, adding they would likely cross the threshold if it does.

The organisation stressed that its preference is for ‘engagement and prevention’ and was not requesting clubs to make ‘bland or risk-free’ content.

However, the EFL warned it is prepared to take ‘proportionate and consistent action’ where ‘conduct which doesn’t meet the standards we expect is repeated or serious.’

Clubs have been asked to ensure a senior leader owns the standard applied to the club’s content, as well as formalising approval arrangements, briefing relevant people and exercising restraint.

#1504. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1503. Nascar, Nets, Big 12 and MSE: Yormark’s appointment and how he can help Milan

AC Milan were introduced to a new name this week: Brett Yormark. But who is he and what does he bring to the table?

With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.
